title: cockatiel: retrying with exponential backoff
intro: Excerpts from cockatiel, a resilience library for JavaScript in the style of .NET's Polly. A RetryPolicy runs a function and, when it fails in a way the policy handles, waits and runs it again, with the wait decided by a pluggable backoff. Start with execute() in RetryPolicy.ts; the backoff strategies are in backoff/.

license.attribution: Adapted from cockatiel (c) 2019 Connor Peet, MIT License. Trimmed for this exercise.

questions.text: Walk through what execute() does when the function fails twice with a handled error and then succeeds, using an ExponentialBackoff.
How does the policy decide whether a failure should be retried at all? What happens to failures it does not handle?
What does decorrelatedJitterGenerator return on each call, and what state does it carry from one call to the next?
Is there anything in how this policy retries that could make an outage of the called service worse? Under what conditions? Point to the lines with a code comment if you can.
Why is a backoff an immutable object whose next() returns a new backoff, rather than a counter kept inside RetryPolicy?
Why does execute() check signal.aborted both before and after waiting for the delay?
How would you make it visible in production that a service is being retried too often or too quickly?
What limits would you add so that retries cannot overwhelm a service that is already struggling?
